papers.title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.41715v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. papers.title: Stochastic Rayleigh-Ritz Ascent: Global Linear Convergence under a Spectral Gap
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.42071v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We consider the adjoint-free random-plane iteration algorithm for finding the top eigenvector of a matrix proposed in (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47 (2026), 1349-1374). Unlike standard methods such as the power method or gradient descent, the above algorithm lacked linear convergence guarantees in the presence of a spectral gap. In this paper, we establish explicit spectral-gap-dependent global linear convergence rates in expectation, providing quantitative guarantees for the empirically observed convergence.

papers.title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.40942v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model.
